$schema_note: v0 scaffold. Roster, polling, fundraising are research-backed. Issue stance scales and personal-fit dimensions are agreed schema. Candidate bios and per-(candidate, issue) positions are TODO and will be filled in via Phase 0 research.

selection_criteria.rule: Include if any one is met: (a) ≥2% in a credible recent poll, (b) ≥$1M cumulative fundraising, (c) holds or has held statewide / major office.

withdrawn.name: Eric Swalwell
withdrawn.note: Suspended following sexual assault and misconduct allegations.

candidates.name: Steve Hilton
candidates.bio_short: Fox News contributor; former host of The Next Revolution (2017–2023); former senior adviser to UK PM David Cameron. Endorsed by Donald Trump (2026-04-06).
candidates.money_raised_note: $6.6M cumulative per April 2026 reporting; CalMatters H2-2025 filing showed $4.1M.

candidates.name: Tom Steyer
candidates.bio_short: Billionaire investor, environmental activist, and 2020 presidential candidate; founder of Farallon Capital and NextGen America. Campaign is largely self-funded.
candidates.money_raised_note: Largely self-funded through April 2026 per CapRadio. On track for most expensive gubernatorial campaign in CA history.

candidates.name: Chad Bianco
candidates.bio_short: Sheriff of Riverside County since 2018; 26-year veteran of the Riverside County Sheriff's Department.
candidates.money_raised_note: Over 10,000 individual donors per CalMatters / theballotbook.com.

candidates.name: Xavier Becerra
candidates.bio_short: Former U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (2021–2025); former Attorney General of California (2017–2021); former U.S. Representative (1993–2017).
candidates.money_raised_note: H2 2025 figure per CalMatters; cumulative through April 2026 likely higher.

candidates.name: Katie Porter
candidates.bio_short: Former U.S. Representative for CA-47 (previously CA-45), 2019–2025; UC Irvine law professor; known nationally for committee-hearing whiteboard explainers.

candidates.name: Matt Mahan
candidates.bio_short: Mayor of San José since 2022; former San José City Council member; former tech executive; moderate Democrat focused on homelessness response and cost-of-living.
candidates.money_raised_note: Leading Democratic non-self-funded candidate per CapRadio April 2026.

candidates.name: Antonio Villaraigosa
candidates.bio_short: Former Mayor of Los Angeles (2005–2013); former Speaker of the California State Assembly (1998–2000). Previously ran for governor in 2018.

endorsements.endorser: Building and Construction Trades Council of California
Peace Officers Research Association of California (PORAC)

candidates.name: Tony Thurmond
candidates.bio_short: California Superintendent of Public Instruction since 2019; former State Assemblymember (Richmond / Contra Costa); former social worker.
candidates.money_raised_note: H2 2025 figure per CalMatters; the lowest reported total in the field.

issues.name: Housing supply & zoning preemption
issues.short_description: How aggressively should the state push to build more housing, including over local objection?
issues.ca_specific_context: Local control under CEQA and city zoning has historically blocked dense infill; recent state law (SB 9, SB 10, SB 423) preempts some of that.

stance_scale.label: Build aggressively — preempt local zoning where it blocks supply
Build a lot — strong state targets, modest preemption
Build with balance — state nudges, local control preserved
Slow growth — protect neighborhood character and existing residents
Focus on subsidies and tenant protections, not supply

issues.name: Homelessness response
issues.short_description: Where should the state's approach to homelessness sit on the enforcement-to-services spectrum?
issues.ca_specific_context: Prop 1 (2024) expanded conservatorship and mental-health funding; cities differ widely on encampment sweeps; SB 43 widened the bar for conservatorship.

stance_scale.label: Aggressive clearance — sweeps and expanded conservatorship as primary tools
Enforcement-first with concurrent service offers
Balanced — enforcement only when shelter/services are available
Housing-first primarily, minimal enforcement
Heavy investment in supportive housing and services; treat enforcement as last resort

issues.name: Middle-income tax rates
issues.short_description: Where should state income tax rates for middle-income earners go?
issues.ca_specific_context: California's progressive income tax has top marginal rate ~13.3%; middle brackets fund the bulk of state services.

stance_scale.label: Significantly cut middle-income tax rates
Modestly cut middle-income rates
Hold current rates
Modestly raise middle-income rates
Significantly raise middle-income rates

issues.name: Top-bracket / corporate / wealth tax
issues.short_description: Should CA raise taxes on top earners, corporations, or introduce a wealth tax?
issues.ca_specific_context: Multiple wealth-tax bills (e.g., AB 259) have been proposed; corporate tax is 8.84%.

stance_scale.label: Cut top-bracket and corporate rates
Hold current top rates
Modestly raise top-bracket and/or corporate rates
Substantially raise top-bracket and corporate rates
Introduce a new state-level wealth tax on highest earners

issues.name: Commercial property tax (Prop 13 split-roll)
issues.short_description: Should commercial property be taxed at market value (split-roll), or stay under Prop 13?
issues.ca_specific_context: Prop 15 (2020) would have implemented a commercial split-roll; failed 52-48.

stance_scale.label: Strengthen Prop 13 protections for commercial property
Hold Prop 13 protections for commercial property
Targeted reforms (e.g., apply only to very large commercial holdings)
Phase in commercial split-roll
Full commercial split-roll — tax commercial at market value

issues.name: Residential Prop 13 protections
issues.short_description: Should residential Prop 13 protections be preserved, narrowed, or rolled back?
issues.ca_specific_context: Prop 13 (1978) caps property tax at 1% of assessed value with limited increases; Prop 19 (2020) restricted parent-child transfers.

stance_scale.label: Strengthen residential Prop 13 protections
Hold current residential protections
Limited reforms (e.g., transfer-rule tweaks)
Significant reforms while preserving primary-home protection
Phase out residential Prop 13

issues.name: Utility rate regulation
issues.short_description: What role should the state play in setting electricity, gas, and insurance rates?
issues.ca_specific_context: PG&E, SCE, SDG&E rates have risen sharply; CPUC reform and proposals to replace investor-owned utilities are active debate.

stance_scale.label: Deregulate — let market and competition set rates
Modest regulation, focus on grid investment
Rate freeze and significant CPUC reform
Public option / break up monopolies
Full state takeover of investor-owned utilities

issues.name: California gas excise tax
issues.short_description: Should CA's gas excise tax be suspended, held, or expanded?
issues.ca_specific_context: SB 1 (2017) raised the tax and earmarked revenue for transportation; current rate among highest in US.

stance_scale.label: Suspend the gas excise tax
Pause scheduled increases
Hold the current rate
Modestly raise the tax for transportation investment
Significantly raise the tax, earmark for climate / transit

issues.name: Fuel and refinery environmental rules
issues.short_description: Should LCFS, refinery emissions rules, and related fuel mandates be loosened, held, or tightened?
issues.ca_specific_context: Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS) and CARB rules push refineries toward lower-carbon fuels; oil industry argues this raises pump prices.

stance_scale.label: Suspend LCFS and refinery environmental rules
Weaken specific rules to lower gas prices
Maintain current rules
Tighten specific rules to accelerate decarbonization
Major expansion of fuel emissions regulation

issues.name: Policing and criminal penalties
issues.short_description: What's the right balance between expanding police capacity, reform, and non-police alternatives?
issues.ca_specific_context: Fentanyl deaths, retail-theft enforcement, and police oversight debates have all driven CA policy since 2024.

stance_scale.label: Significantly expand law enforcement and toughen penalties
Expand law enforcement with modest reforms
Mixed approach — more officers AND more accountability/diversion
Prioritize reform, oversight, and non-police alternatives
Substantially shift funding from policing to community services

issues.name: Prop 36 / Prop 47 direction
issues.short_description: Should CA go further on rolling back Prop 47, hold Prop 36 as passed, or restore Prop 47?
issues.ca_specific_context: Prop 47 (2014) reduced certain felonies to misdemeanors; Prop 36 (2024) rolled back parts of that; implementation is still in progress.

stance_scale.label: Go further than Prop 36 — significantly toughen penalties
Implement Prop 36 fully, consider further toughening
Implement Prop 36 as passed; no further changes
Implement narrowly; advocate restoring some Prop 47 protections
Restore Prop 47 in full; expand diversion programs

issues.name: Sanctuary and immigration enforcement
issues.short_description: What should CA's posture be on cooperation with federal immigration enforcement?
issues.ca_specific_context: SB 54 (2017) limits state cooperation with ICE; under renewed federal pressure as of 2025–2026.

stance_scale.label: Repeal SB 54; full ICE cooperation
Allow specific exceptions to SB 54
Maintain SB 54 as-is
Expand sanctuary protections (e.g., legal defense funding)
Major expansion — state-level immigration protections including state ID

issues.name: Climate goals and decarbonization timeline
issues.short_description: Should the state's net-zero-by-2045 target be accelerated, held, or softened?
issues.ca_specific_context: AB 1279 (2022) codified net-zero-by-2045; interim milestones are in flux.

stance_scale.label: Repeal or significantly soften the 2045 target
Slow the timeline; allow more flexibility
Hold the 2045 target with current implementation
Accelerate the timeline (e.g., to 2040)
Major acceleration (e.g., 2035) with binding interim milestones

issues.name: Nuclear power's role in CA's grid
issues.short_description: Expand, hold, or phase out nuclear power in California?
issues.ca_specific_context: Diablo Canyon's life was extended in 2022; no new plants currently planned.

stance_scale.label: Expand significantly — site new plants; extend existing
Extend Diablo Canyon and similar; keep options open
Maintain status quo (current Diablo extension only)
Wind down existing plants on current schedule
Accelerate phase-out of all nuclear

issues.name: Natural gas as bridge fuel
issues.short_description: What role should natural gas play during the energy transition?
issues.ca_specific_context: Natural gas peaker plants and building-gas hookups are both contested; SoCalGas / PG&E gas systems are aging.

stance_scale.label: Expand natural gas infrastructure and use
Maintain current natural gas role; gradual phase-down
Stable status; let market and reliability needs decide
Phase out natural gas in power generation by mid-2030s
Aggressive natural gas phase-out across all sectors

issues.name: Oil and gas production in CA
issues.short_description: Should in-state oil and gas extraction expand, hold, or phase down?
issues.ca_specific_context: SB 1137 (2022) established 3,200-ft setbacks; ballot fight overturned and re-affirmed; Kern County is the production heartland.

stance_scale.label: Expand in-state oil and gas production
Maintain current production levels; reduce regulation
Status quo — current setbacks and permitting
Phase down — tighten setbacks, halt new permits
Rapid phase-out of in-state extraction

issues.name: Water storage and conveyance projects
issues.short_description: What should CA's posture be on Delta tunnel, new dams, and major water infrastructure?
issues.ca_specific_context: Delta Conveyance Project, Sites Reservoir, and Pacheco Reservoir are all in various permitting stages.

stance_scale.label: Expand all major projects — Delta tunnel, new dams, conveyance
Pursue most major projects with environmental modifications
Pursue selected projects case-by-case
Pause major new construction; focus on existing infrastructure
Halt major new water infrastructure projects

issues.name: Water allocations (ag vs. urban vs. environmental)
issues.short_description: How should CA balance water among agriculture, urban use, and environmental flows?
issues.ca_specific_context: Roughly 80% of human-developed water goes to agriculture; environmental flows, Delta salinity, and groundwater recharge are competing claims.

stance_scale.label: Prioritize agriculture — protect water rights, ease environmental flows
Favor agriculture with modest environmental considerations
Balance among ag, urban, and environmental needs
Favor urban and environmental with ag concessions
Prioritize environmental flows and urban use over ag

issues.name: CEQA reform
issues.short_description: Should CEQA's environmental review requirements be rolled back, preserved, or strengthened?
issues.ca_specific_context: CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act) is widely blamed for project delays; multiple targeted reform bills (e.g., AB 1633, SB 423) have passed since 2023.

stance_scale.label: Major rollback — broad statutory exemptions
Significant exemptions for housing and infrastructure
Targeted exemptions, case-by-case
Preserve CEQA with minor procedural reforms
Strengthen CEQA's environmental review requirements

issues.name: K-12 school funding and governance
issues.short_description: Should CA increase, hold, or restructure K-12 funding?
issues.ca_specific_context: Prop 98 (1988) sets a minimum funding floor; LCFF (2013) restructured allocation around student need.

stance_scale.label: Significantly cut K-12 spending
Hold or modestly trim spending
Maintain current spending levels
Modest funding increases (teacher pay, facilities)
Major new funding via dedicated tax or bond

issues.name: School choice and charters
issues.short_description: Should CA expand charter schools and school choice, or restrict them?
issues.ca_specific_context: AB 1505 (2019) gave districts more charter denial authority; vouchers have repeatedly failed at the ballot.

stance_scale.label: Significantly expand charters and school choice (including vouchers)
Expand charters; protect parental choice
Maintain the current charter framework
Restrict charter expansion
Cap or freeze charter growth; redirect funding to public schools

issues.name: Healthcare funding mechanism
issues.short_description: If state-level single-payer healthcare is on the table, how should it be funded?
issues.ca_specific_context: AB 1400 / CalCare proposals have repeatedly stalled over funding; Medi-Cal was expanded to undocumented adults in 2024.

stance_scale.label: Roll back recent Medi-Cal expansions
Hold current system; focus on cost containment
Incremental Medi-Cal / ACA expansion, no new broad tax
State single-payer, funded primarily by wealth and corporate taxes
State single-payer with broad new taxation (payroll, VAT-style)

issues.name: Abortion and reproductive rights
issues.short_description: Should CA expand, hold, or restrict abortion access?
issues.ca_specific_context: Prop 1 (2022) enshrined abortion rights in the CA Constitution; CA has funded travel for out-of-state patients.

stance_scale.label: Significant restrictions (gestational limits, parental consent)
Permit some restrictions
Hold current CA protections (Prop 1)
Strong defense — expand access funding and provider network
Major expansion — constitutional amendment beyond Prop 1; fund out-of-state patients; broaden providers

issues.name: Gun policy
issues.short_description: Should CA's gun laws be loosened, held, or expanded?
issues.ca_specific_context: CA's assault-weapons ban, magazine limits, and CCW frameworks have been in continuous litigation since Bruen (2022).

stance_scale.label: Significant rollback (looser concealed-carry, ease assault-weapons enforcement)
Loosen specific restrictions
Hold current CA gun laws
Strong defense of current laws; close loopholes
Major expansion of restrictions (registry, supply controls, additional bans)

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Wealth and self-funding
personal_fit_dimensions.description: How much do a candidate's personal wealth and self-funding of their campaign matter to you?

scale.label: Strongly prefer wealthy / self-funded (independent of donors)

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Conflict orientation
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Do you prefer a candidate who acts as a pragmatic dealmaker, or a principled fighter?

scale.label: Strongly prefer principled fighter / outspoken critic

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Federal vs. state focus
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Should the next governor focus on California's own problems, or actively confront the federal government?

scale.label: Strongly state-focused — keep DC fights out of CA governance
Strongly prefer willingness to confront the Trump administration

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Position consistency
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Do you weight consistent positions over time, or are you open to candidates whose positions have evolved?

scale.label: Strongly value candidates who update based on new information

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Integrity and controversy record
personal_fit_dimensions.description: How much do prior scandals, ethics investigations, or controversies factor into your decision?

scale.label: Past controversies do not influence me

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Electability
personal_fit_dimensions.description: How much does general-election viability — polling strength, fundraising, broad appeal — factor in?

scale.label: Decisive — I weight electability above other factors
Does not factor in — I vote on alignment regardless of viability

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Years in elected office
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Do you prefer a fresh political voice, or someone with extensive elected-office tenure?

scale.label: Strongly prefer fresh — under 5 years in elected office
Strongly prefer extensive — 15+ years in elected office

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Career background
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Which career backgrounds appeal to you in a governor? (Leave blank for no preference.)

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Demographic background
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Which candidate backgrounds matter positively to you? (Optional — leave blank for no preference. Your answers are anonymous.)

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Geographic background
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Do you prefer a candidate from a particular region of California? (Leave blank for no preference.)

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Age / generation
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Which age cohort do you prefer? (Optional.)

personal_fit_dimensions.name: Endorser coalition
personal_fit_dimensions.description: Whose endorsement signal matters most to you? (Leave blank for no preference.)

options.label: Major California newspapers (LA Times, SF Chronicle, Sac Bee)
